title: H₂: covalent–ionic mixing
summary: Build two singlet structures and see how on-site electron repulsion changes their weights.
steps: Construct a covalent singlet and a symmetric ionic structure from spin-resolved determinants.
Ask symvb for the symbolic Hamiltonian and overlap matrices.
Set h = −1, overlap s = 0.25, and U = 4; solve the generalized eigenproblem and evaluate Chirgwin–Coulson weights.
tryIt: Change U_value to 0 or 12. At zero repulsion the weights are equal; increasing U suppresses the ionic contribution.
scope: A two-structure, on-site-repulsion teaching model. Energies are in |h| units; this is not an ab initio H₂ potential-energy curve.
code:
import sympy as sp
import numpy as np
from scipy.linalg import eigh
from symvb import Molecule, FixedPsi, System

# Change these parameters, then run again.
U_value = 4
s_value = 0.25
h_value = -1

m = Molecule(
    zero_ii=True, interacting_orbs=['ab'],
    subst={'h': ('H_ab',), 's': ('S_ab',)},
    max_2e_centers=1,
)
covalent = FixedPsi('aB')
covalent.add_str_det('bA', coef=1)
ionic = FixedPsi('aA')
ionic.add_str_det('bB', coef=1)
H, S = System.from_structures(m, [covalent, ionic]).hamiltonian()
h, s, U = sp.symbols('h s U')
# Name the two on-site repulsion integrals explicitly.
H = H.subs({sp.Symbol('T_aaaa'): U, sp.Symbol('T_bbbb'): U})
show_math('Hamiltonian in the covalent / ionic basis', H)
show_math('Overlap matrix', S)

values = {h: h_value, s: s_value, U: U_value}
Hn = np.array(H.subs(values), dtype=float)
Sn = np.array(S.subs(values), dtype=float)
energies, vectors = eigh(Hn, Sn)
c = vectors[:, 0]
weights = c * (Sn @ c)
show_math('Ground-state energy', sp.Eq(sp.Symbol('E_0'), sp.Float(energies[0], 7)))
show_math('Covalent and ionic weights', sp.Matrix([float(x) for x in weights]).evalf(6))
print(f'Covalent: {100*weights[0]:.2f}% | Ionic: {100*weights[1]:.2f}%')
print('Weights include the nonorthogonal overlap metric.')

math.label: Hamiltonian in the covalent / ionic basis
math.tex: \left[\begin{matrix}4 h s & 4 h\\4 h & 2 U + 4 h s\end{matrix}\right]

expected.stdout:
Covalent: 80.96% | Ionic: 19.04%
Weights include the nonorthogonal overlap metric.

title: H₂⁺: a one-electron bond
summary: Derive the bonding and antibonding energies for one electron shared by two orbitals.
steps: Use the localized one-electron states a and b as the basis.
Build H and S with an orbital overlap s and site energy eps.
Solve det(H − ES) = 0, then evaluate the two roots for a chosen overlap.
tryIt: Change s_value from 0.2 to 0.4, keeping h = −1 and eps = 0. Compare how the bonding and antibonding energies respond.
scope: An effective one-electron model with equal site energies. Orbital overlap must satisfy |s| < 1; energies use the same units as h and eps.
code:
import sympy as sp
from symvb import Molecule, hamiltonian
from symvb.fixed_psi import generate_dets

s_value = 0.2
m = Molecule(
    zero_ii=False, interacting_orbs=['ab'],
    subst={'h': ('H_ab',), 'eps': ('H_aa', 'H_bb'), 's': ('S_ab',)},
)
basis = generate_dets(1, 0, 2)
H, S = hamiltonian(m, basis, two_electron=False)
h, s, eps, E = sp.symbols('h s eps E')
show_math('Hamiltonian', H)
show_math('Overlap matrix', S)
roots = sp.solve((H - E*S).det(), E)
# Identify the bonding branch at a specified physical reference point.
reference = {h: -1, eps: 0, s: sp.Rational(1, 5)}
roots.sort(key=lambda root: float(root.subs(reference)))
show_math('Bonding energy', sp.Eq(sp.Symbol('E_+'), sp.factor(roots[0])))
show_math('Antibonding energy', sp.Eq(sp.Symbol('E_-'), sp.factor(roots[1])))
values = {h: -1, eps: 0, s: s_value}
for label, root in zip(['Bonding', 'Antibonding'], roots):
    print(f'{label}: {float(root.subs(values)):.6f} at s = {s_value}')

expected.stdout:
Bonding: -0.833333 at s = 0.2
Antibonding: 1.250000 at s = 0.2

title: Allyl radical: two resonance structures
summary: Construct two covalent Rumer structures and calculate their overlap, energies, and equal mixing weights.
steps: Pair the a–b orbitals into a singlet, leaving an unpaired electron on c; then make the equivalent b–c pairing.
Build the two-structure Hamiltonian and overlap matrix with symvb.
Compare one localized structure with their symmetric combination, including the overlap metric.
tryIt: Set s_value to 0, 0.2, and 0.4. In this covalent-only one-electron model, the resonance stabilization vanishes at zero orbital overlap.
scope: Allyl radical, three orbitals and three electrons. This restricted covalent-only, one-electron model omits ionic structures and electron repulsion; it is distinct from the allyl-anion model in the symvb paper.
code:
import sympy as sp
from symvb import Molecule, FixedPsi, hamiltonian
from symvb.system import chirgwin_coulson

s_value = 0.2
m = Molecule.chain(3, hubbard=False)
R1 = FixedPsi('aBc', coupled_pairs=[(0, 1)])
R2 = FixedPsi('aBc', coupled_pairs=[(1, 2)])
H, S = hamiltonian(m, [R1, R2], two_electron=False)
h, s = sp.symbols('h s')
show_math('Hamiltonian over R1 and R2', H)
show_math('Overlap over R1 and R2', S)
show_math('Normalized structure overlap', sp.simplify(S[0,1]/S[0,0]))

# Symmetry gives equal coefficients for the bonding combination.
c = sp.Matrix([1, 1])
E_one = sp.simplify(H[0,0]/S[0,0])
E_res = sp.simplify((c.T*H*c)[0]/(c.T*S*c)[0])
resonance = sp.simplify(E_one - E_res)
weights = chirgwin_coulson(c, S, simplify=True)
show_math('Energy of one structure', E_one)
show_math('Energy of the symmetric combination', E_res)
show_math('Resonance stabilization: E(one) − E(mixed)', resonance)
show_math('R1 and R2 weights', sp.Matrix(weights))
values = {h: -1, s: s_value}
print(f'E(one) = {float(E_one.subs(values)):.6f}')
print(f'E(mixed) = {float(E_res.subs(values)):.6f}')
print(f'Stabilization = {float(resonance.subs(values)):.6f} |h|')
print('At s = 0 this restricted model is degenerate; the equal mixture is not unique.')

math.label: Hamiltonian over R1 and R2
math.tex: \left[\begin{matrix}2 h s & 4 h s\\4 h s & 2 h s\end{matrix}\right]

expected.stdout:
E(one) = -0.196078
E(mixed) = -0.384615
Stabilization = 0.188537 |h|
At s = 0 this restricted model is degenerate; the equal mixture is not unique.
